close_reason: Added DeviationAddError::MalformedScope variant + validate_scope() helper called by DeviationStore::add. Malformed scopes (missing required props, wrong-typed props) for the canonical scope kinds (any, issuer_dn_contains, issuer_dn_exact, serial_range) now produce a specific error at insertion time naming the offending kind and the structural problem, instead of silently never matching at evaluation time. The operator-perception bug ('my deviation isn't being applied') is now caught at the API boundary. Custom / caller-defined scope kinds are accepted without inspection (the documented fail-closed extensibility contract). Six regression tests cover the canonical kinds: missing prop on issuer_dn_contains, wrong-typed prop on issuer_dn_contains, missing prop on issuer_dn_exact, missing prop on serial_range, well-formed scopes pass, custom kinds pass. Considered option (a) make-fields-private but rejected: the public-field shape is needed for the OSCAL serde shape, and PKIX-hy2e.22's #[non_exhaustive] already blocks the external struct-literal construction path; the remaining hand-built malformed scope path is hit at insertion-time validation. 265 lib tests + 7 doc tests pass; clippy --all-features --all-targets clean.
description: Site: deviation.rs:444-495. DeviationScope::matches returns false for: (a) unknown kind, (b) missing required prop, (c) wrong-typed prop, (d) malformed DER. All four also produce false from a legitimate 'this cert is not within scope' result. Scenario: an operator hand-edits an OSCAL Risk JSON file and forgets the issuer_dn_substring prop. Parse-time validation catches MOST shape errors, but the deviation.rs side itself doesn't reject — it accepts a hand-constructed DeviationScope { kind: SCOPE_KIND_ISSUER_DN_CONTAINS, props: vec![] } via direct struct literal (which is publicly accessible — props and kind are pub fields). DeviationScope::matches against any cert returns false. Maintenance consequence: 'my deviation isn't being applied' tickets where the cause is a silently malformed scope; no way to distinguish from 'cert isn't in scope.' Fix: either (a) make kind and props non-pub and force construction through validating constructors only (breaking change but the scope of breakage is small at 0.x); (b) split DeviationScope::matches return type into Result<bool, ScopeError> where ScopeError covers the malformed cases; (c) log a warning at first encounter. (a) is the right answer pre-1.0. The deviation.rs tests cover the fail-closed behavior but do not cover the operator-perception 'I configured this and it doesn't work' angle.
title: DeviationScope::matches fail-closed on missing prop is indistinguishable from no-match
